questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Culinary experiences, cultural history, financial aspects and recommendations from friends.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My personal experience was brilliant. However, the level of education in Korea is not as high as I expected, which made the academic part of the exchange below my expectations.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. However, there is a lot of work connected to going abroad, so it required patience and dedication.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A fair amount at orientation. The most well-functioning part was, that the university had a really good program for the social lives of exchange students, which I highly advise other Ewha expats to join.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Others should join the EWHA PEACE BUDDY program.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my housing on AirBnB, and it was relatively easy. However, EWHA does provide suggestions for off-campus housing which I did not see before I had already booked. I think you could save a fair amount of money booking through that instead of AirBnB. However, I do not know if the quality of the housing is as good, as I dont know anyone who did it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I think the amount of private life is probably way better off-campus, and living two people in the same room (on campus) might not be for everyone. It also depend on which roommate you will get. However, it creates the urge to spend more energy on social relations at first, since you dont live near the other exchange students. 
It is also important to notice, that you will pay more for off-campus housing, also in transportation to and from the university. However, it can be a good way to experience other parts of the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I'm sure it was fine and the prices was good, but I can't say since I stayed off-campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of documents was needed and hard to get. Also, some things was hard to find in english.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
To be honest, it is very far back in my memory. I can sort of recall me having to find a bunch of documents from KU, having them signes by the right people etc. etc. 
However, EWHA's communication channel and personnel are very helpful with any and all questions.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, two coordinators where constantly available, making the application experience way easier.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got very lucky and got all the classes I wanted. However, the process is first come - first served, making it very stressful, and I talked to many who did not get classes they wanted or needed desperately to accord to their home institutions demands.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to have backup classes, talk to your home institution about what courses they would approve, do a pre-approval application for various courses and educate yourself about the application process. That helped me a lot!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Some courses were great, others a complete waste of time. 
It is swing and a miss with courses abroad, but I would advise people to educate themselves and ask former expats about different courses and professors before applying for courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Some courses were theoretical, applied critical thinking and were super interesting.
Others were way, way to easy, uninteresting and to be honest, some of them provided middle- and high school level education. The level in Korea is definitely lower than in Denmark, and at the time of writing I have received straight A's with less engagement than in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Depends on the professor.
Mostly it was lectures as in Denmark. However, I also had online classes, which was convenient as an expat, but less fruitful.
Some professors were theoretical and critical, whilst others just provided random facts, not focusing on critical thinking. I found this highly problematic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociology of Crime
Social Psychology
Politics of North Korea
Child Welfare
Cultural Diversity and Social Welfare

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sociology of Crime - the professor is very talented, interesting and somewhat challenging (in a good way).
Social Psychology - Same professor as the first course and same reasons. 
Politics of North Korea - I think all students going to Korea should take a similar course. Learning about political differences and culture in Korea is very rewarding and interesting.

Personal spending DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transport is super cheap, which is nice - same with taxis.
NHIS (mandatory Korean health insurance) is quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think there are a bunch of clubs etc. However, they all require applications and seem a bit picky with who they allow in, so I did not apply for any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Music hall with concerts, different conferences, PEACE BUDDY social program, sports facilities, lots of food, church and gym.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Again, EWHA PEACE BUDDY program is a great way to meet people in the first weeks, and they plan stuff like sports day, movie night, a party etc.
They also partner you with a Korean student who helps adjusting to life in Korea which is super nice.
Also - go out to eat as much as you can. It is cheap and very good food is available everywhere.
Experience the culture in museums, sport games, concerts etc. It is very cool and accesible.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I think it is important to go outside of Seoul relatively often, so your everyday life does not become to trivial. 
I went to Japan, Busan, Jeju and Taipei, and all of my trips were wonderful experiences!
Also it is common to visit the DMZ near the border of North Korea, also very worthy of visiting.
many students also to Temple stays, which I think might be cool - I did not have the time unfortunately.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Due to the fact that I have been traveling a lot around Asia, I found it very easy to adjust to the local culture. I think it might be harder for some people, but South Korea is very developed and super easy to figure out.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the PEACE BUDDY Program or similar social clubs promoting bond between expats and locals!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
There is a language barrier,  but google translate helps a lot here :)
I did not find any cultural differences super challenging myself.
However, there is something of a drinking culture, which can be overwhelming for some - so be aware when you go out. Also, Koreans outside the Uni rarely interacts with foreigners, so do not expect to meet a lot of Koreans randomly around bars etc.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the prices, the weird stuff and most of all - Noerebang (Karaoke).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Put a lot of effort into socializing the first few weeks of your exchange, and don't be shy. Everyone is feeling out of their comfort zone so just talk to people - it pays of!
2. Join the PEACE BUDDY program for an easy transition into life in Korea.
3. Do not expect Korean students to interact with you a lot. Many of them are shy and introverted around foreign students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Spend energy on finding courses suitable for you. If possible, find a student who went to EWHA before and ask them for tips!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was definitely the people I met. Having friends from all over the world and experiencing a lot of different cultures is a privilige, and I recommend it to everyone!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
A mix of two things I think.
1. Feelings of exclusion from one group I hung out with. However, I decided to just ditch the people I found exclusive in that group and focused on other friends, which made my stay way better! Listen to yourself and do not waste time on people you dont like - you are on exchange for you and not any other person!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO TO KOREA!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
